description: Reconstruction of July 1863 as the base of the two main maps (desktop and phone): the Mapbox satellite style is replaced by an inline style that draws only the local tile pyramid /tiles1863/v1-65d491b8/ over a neutral ground colour; permanent label, "Show what was changed" toggle, sources link; the product's road/stream/farm overlays are redrawn from the catalogue geometry. The Walkthrough map is untouched. Needs the overlay files of tools/t0/base1863/stage_assets.py and the service-worker and headers additions of tools/t0/base1863/b63_build.py (BASE1863-README.md). [Release 1 integration 2026-10-20: the generator at HEAD also emits patches that move the Virtual Walkthrough map and seven sub-pages to the reconstruction and REMOVE the Street View embed and the Soldier's Eye View (B63:walkthrough-style, streetview-embed, soldiers-eye-*, page-*); those are left out of this file pending an owner decision (standing rule: do not break the Virtual Walkthrough; no feature is dropped without the owner).]

patches.note: inserts the runtime const GTB63 before T4 (the function that adds the product's own layers to a main map) and draws the road labels from the catalogue geometry
stream labels from the NHD catalogue courses
farm labels at the documented farmhouse points
after the product layers exist: road/stream/farm-outline lines start hidden, labels sorted by rank, data applied
the desktop main map: inline style with the local reconstruction instead of the Mapbox satellite style
the phone main map (the Walkthrough map has its own style string and is NOT touched)
the Layers panel starts in the state the map is in (the road and stream lines are hidden on the reconstruction base, see BASE1863-README.md section 6)
there is no farm boundary in the catalogue: the old rectangles did not even contain their farmhouse (Rose: 347 m off), so the row is removed

patches.find: unfold on a real satellite map
patches.repl: unfold on a map of the battlefield reconstructed as it was in July 1863 (not a photograph)
patches.note: the page copy no longer says the base is a satellite map
